data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's own terms not as an inductive inference that the theory is more likely true, but as a critical rational choice to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe tests, acknowledging that this choice carries no guarantee of future success and costs the agent any claim to probabilistic security.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If the preference implies an expectation that the theory will continue to succeed based solely on past success, it smuggles in induction.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) is required to justify the preference, the Tichý-Miller theorem undermines the defense within Popper's formal framework.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the choice between multiple unrefuted theories cannot be made without assigning differential weight based on past performance, the distinction between corroboration and probability collapses.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "Critical Rational Choice via Severe Testing: The mechanism distinguishes between the logical status of a theory (which remains conjectural) and the methodological rule for action. Preference is justified by the degree of 'corroboration' (a report on past performance under severe tests), which serves as a non-probabilistic indicator of a theory's resilience. The agent chooses the 'fittest' survivor not because it is probable, but because it is the best available target for further criticism and the most reliable guide for action given the current state of knowledge, explicitly rejecting the induction that past success ensures future success. It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": []}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
